Mandobar, Yohanis Kadiwaru): auq_1 'Elicitation of first word list and sociolinguistic information' (auq_1.wav +, a 5-page 226-item English/Indonesian/Korur word list), auq_8 'Elicitation of word lists, possessive constructions and simple phrases' (wav), 'Elicitation of sociolinguistic information', 'Introductory text of Korur community', 'Conversation about importance of customary land', two self-introductions.
sources.note: The PDF (LibreOffice Calc export dated 2023-01-26, columns 'English gloss | Indonesian gloss | Korur') contains no legend, transcription note or prose of any kind. 27 of the 226 Korur forms carry an acute accent and in every case it sits on the word-final syllable: dornó 'wrist', kedé 'blue', efeyéf 'red', erensé 'fly', erinyá 'branch', metá 'cloud/sharp', firó 'feather', nemtá 'green', mefná 'hot', merá 'far', mofín 'woman', moworí 'old', ne-sabór 'to sing', nerté 'dirty', bereké 'unripe (coconut)', mesó 'ripe', sokó 'thumb', sombó 'sun', timót 'person/man', tenggeré 'hand', wokó 'root'; the…

sources.citation: Grace, George W. 1970. Notes on the phonological history of the Austronesian languages of the Sarmi Coast. University of Hawaii Working Papers in Linguistics 2(9): 55-104 (ERIC ED054658) [pre-publication of Oceanic Linguistics 10: 11-37, 1971, doi:10.2307/3622831].
sources.note: Nothing. Diachronic study of consonant/vowel correspondences and canonical forms for Sobei, Wakde, Masimasi, Anus, Bonggo, Tarpia from Grace's own short vocabularies; no mention of stress, accent, tone or prosody anywhere in the text (a full-text search for stress/accent + intro read).

sources.citation: Grace, George W. 1955. 'Doris Day' field notebook no. 7: Anus (heading 'koru fanu / anus'). Handwritten ms., 8 pp. (cover + 7 pp.): pronouns, numerals, c. 150 lexical items and short verb/possessive paradigms elicited through Malay, many forms carrying a stress mark. The George Grace linguistic research and slides of Melanesia collection, 1955-1956, item 17. Honolulu: University of Hawai'i at Manoa Library (PARADISEC finding aid GG1-01).
sources.note: No prose on prosody anywhere in the 8 pages. Stress is MARKED (raised vertical stroke before the stressed syllable) on a good share of the elicited forms, e.g. p.3 dou 'nasarir / ik 'kaserir / e 'sarir 'walk', ik 'kama / dou 'nama 'come', 'mokrit 'belly', 'tiwo 'bone'; p.4 sa'war 'blood', 'benem 'neck', ti'mot 'person', mo'fin 'woman'; p.7 'fowo 'fruit', sim'ro 'flower'; p.8 'bafu 'ashes', 'kaimefra 'black', 'yatinea 'big', do'bo 'short', me'ra(ia) 'long', men'se 'thin', me'te'ri 'thick', me'fna 'hot', mesro'di 'slippery', mema'fo 'heavy'. Marks fall on initial, medial and final syllables, so…
